dimensions.rationale: At the reported sink the fix is at the correct trust boundary — canonicalize then verify containment before any filesystem use — not a caller/symptom guard; it just isn't replicated at the sibling sinks.

Verified in-tree: PythonDistributionAnalyzer.java:216 -> ExtractionUtil.extractFilesUsingFilter; ExtractionUtil.extractFile accepts on `filter.accept(file.getParentFile(), file.getName())`, so a .whl entry named `../../../METADATA` passes the name-only filter and writes outside the destination.

dimensions.rationale: Textbook CWE-022 defense-of-record — canonicalize (resolving symlinks and ..) then verify the target stays under the base dir — and the boundary check is strictly stronger than the official fix's raw prefix test.
dimensions.evidence: `filePath.equals(destinationPath) || filePath.startsWith(destinationPath + File.separator)` closes the sibling-prefix bypass (e.g. dest=/tmp/dest, target=/tmp/dest-evil/x) that the official `f.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(destPath)` still admits; canonicalization also defeats absolute-path entries and symlink-through-earlier-entry attacks.
dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: ExtractionUtil.java is entirely unpatched, leaving a live path to the same CVE-2018-12036 traversal. Verified reachable: PythonDistributionAnalyzer.java:216 calls ExtractionUtil.extractFilesUsingFilter(...) -> extractArchive -> extractFile, which builds `new File(destination, entry.getName())` and gates only on `filter.accept(file.getParentFile(), file.getName())` — a name-only filter. A malicious .whl/.egg entry named `../../../../METADATA` matches the filter and is written outside the destination. The official fix adds canonical-path containment checks at ExtractionUtil.extractFiles, extractArchive, and extractFile precisely for this.

The gzip/bzip2 branches of ArchiveAnalyzer.extractFiles (`new File(destination, GzipUtils.getUncompressedFilename(archive.getName()))` / BZip2Utils equivalent, ~lines 412/425) get no containment check, whereas the official fix adds one to both. Practical exploitability is low because File.getName() strips path separators, but this is an official-fixed location our patch leaves unguarded.

No execution evidence supports the patch. pov_before_reproduced=false means the POV never demonstrated the vulnerability on the unpatched build, so pov_after_still_reproduces=false proves nothing; regressions_ran=0 means no test at all exercised the new guard or checked for behavioral regressions. The compile-safety and no-over-restriction conclusions above come from reading the base tree, not from a green build.

result.root_cause: Archive entry names are attacker-controlled and are joined to the extraction directory (`new File(destination, entry.getName())`) and written without ever verifying that the resolved real path stays inside that directory, so `../` or absolute-path entries escape the intended extraction root (Zip Slip).
result.summary: Our patch applies the correct defense-of-record at the reported sink: it canonicalizes both the destination and the resolved entry target and rejects anything not equal to, or a separator-bounded descendant of, the destination — a strictly stronger boundary check than the official fix's raw `startsWith(destPath)`, which admits sibling-prefix directories. It is minimal, fail-closed, and compiles cleanly against the existing `catch (IOException | AnalysisException)` in extractArchive. However, it fixes only 1 of the 5 locations the official fix hardened: ExtractionUtil.java is untouched, and its extractFile sink is genuinely reachable via PythonDistributionAnalyzer -> extractFilesUsingFilter with a name-only filter, so the CWE-022 class survives outside the traced path. Combined with zero execution evidence (the POV never reproduced pre-patch and no regression tests ran), this is a well-built but incomplete fix.
